Redwood AE/SE covered hosting vs dedicated options, egress/billing implications, and SSO/KMS integration. Action items assigned for legal redlines, cost modeling, and a follow-up gating call.
transcript:
Meeting header: Recorded 2025-07-15 14:00 PDT | Duration ~48m | Attendees: Sophie (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Anika (CSM), Olivia (Hera - Procurement), Daniel (Hera - Legal), Priya (Hera - Security), Ethan (Hera - Eng), Samir (Hera - Finance)

[00:00] Sophie (Redwood): ok everyone thanks for joining, um we're calling this a billing and data sovereignty gatecall so quick intros, i'll kick off — i'm sophie, ae at redwood, marco is our se, anika is csm. olivia, daniel?
[00:10] Olivia (Hera): hi yeah olivia here, procurement. thanks, we'll be tight on time — we have finance on the line.
[00:18] Daniel (Hera): daniel here, legal counsel, quick clarifying q: is this only DPA/MSA or will we touch sla termination language?
[00:24] Sophie (Redwood): good call — we'll hit both, plus billing pathways; if anything we can drill into indemnity afterwards.
[00:30] Marco (Redwood): hi all, i'll focus on hosting modes, egress and pilot costs — quick caveat transcription might mess kv cache as K V cash in the notes, ignore that.
[00:40] Priya (Hera): and i want to confirm where data at rest will live; we have a strict EU data residency req for PHI adjacent logs.

[02:05] Sophie (Redwood): quick agenda: 1) procurement approval path & PO timing, 2) DPA/msa exceptions + data residency, 3) sla/uplift and termination language, 4) billing and egress modeling for pilot, 5) next steps. any additions?
[02:16] Samir (Hera): finance will need a sample invoice layout and expected monthly burn, and any potential egress fees called out.

[04:10] Olivia (Hera): current procurement flow is two approvals: procurement + finance, then legal signoff. our target is to get pilot PO by mid-aug but depends on legal.
[04:30] Sophie (Redwood): great — that's in line with what we've seen. we'll send a simplified pricing sheet.

[06:00] Marco (Redwood): on hosting options: hosted api (fastest) vs dedicated reserved capacity (predictable throughput) vs private (vpc/on-prem). For a pilot we usually recommend hosted with contractual data residency or dedicated depending on throughput needs.
[06:25] Ethan (Hera): for the pilot we expect 500k tokens/day peak, uncertain steady state; latency matters for production but pilot can tolerate 200-400ms.
[06:40] Marco (Redwood): that keeps you in hosted for sure; dedicated only if you want strict isolation or long-term commit to lower unit cost. Also note egress: if you route payloads cross-region there is cloud egress plus our transfer fees — we'll show both.

[09:12] Daniel (Hera): on the DPA, primary legal asks: 1) data residency guarantee (EU-only), 2) breach notification SLA 72 hours, 3) carveouts for security telemetry which we may want off by default.
[09:28] Sophie (Redwood): we can accept an EU processing addendum and commit to region pinning for customer data. breach notification 72 hours is standard, we can confirm. for telemetry, our default is to not log customer payloads for hosted customers if requested — we can add opt-out.

[12:00] Priya (Hera): KMS integration is critical — we need to use our HSM KMS in the EU region, and we need proof of key separation for logs. is that supported?
[12:18] Marco (Redwood): yes we support BYOK via KMS for Private and Dedicated, for hosted we have customer-managed keys with our KMS provider in some regions; we'll detail HSM options in the doc. small caveat — full BYOK on hosted has some constraints; we'll list them.

[15:05] Samir (Hera): about pricing: do you have a cap or an overage alert model? finance needs a spend guard for pilot so we don't get surprise invoices.
[15:20] Sophie (Redwood): we can set spend guards, hard caps, and per-route quotas. we'll also provide a forecast spreadsheet with token estimates and egress scenarios.

[18:40] Marco (Redwood): two billing notes: 1) in-hosted model you pay per-token + regional egress; 2) dedicated pools are reserved monthly commitment, lower per-token but upfront commit; 3) private deployments are licensed. We'll put example numbers for your 500k token/day profile.
[19:10] Olivia (Hera): will that example show a worst-case cross-region egress line item?
[19:17] Marco (Redwood): yes — we'll show best case (region pinned) vs worst case (cross-region failover).

[22:00] Daniel (Hera): SLA questions: uptime % targets, credits for outages, and termination for convenience notice periods. we prefer a 99.9% target with credits; termination needs 30-60 days.
[22:18] Sophie (Redwood): our standard SLA offers 99.9% for hosted with credits; Dedicated can be 99.95 depending on contract. termination windows can be negotiated; we'll flag recommended language and your options.

[25:30] Priya (Hera): audit logs - we need immutable access logs for at least 12 months, and access export for quarterly audits. can redwood provide that and grant read access for our auditors?
[25:50] Marco (Redwood): yes, audit logs and export are supported; for hosted customers we have retention tiers as an add-on. for private/dedicated you control retention. we'll attach a sample audit log export spec.

[28:44] Ethan (Hera): technical question: the kv cache reference earlier — how does that affect PII leakage risk? our app stores pointers to PHI, need assurance it doesn't leak in model outputs.
[29:05] Marco (Redwood): good question — our runtime isolates KV cache per customer; we also have filters and evaluation hooks. but legal side should consider training/retain language; we commit not to use customer data to train models unless explicitly opted-in. we'll add explicit non-training clause in DPA.

[31:10] Daniel (Hera): indemnity — our counsel wants mutual indemnity with a cap tied to fees; you usually have carveouts for third-party components — we need to align.
[31:28] Sophie (Redwood): we can propose mutual indemnity with standard carveouts; we'll submit a starting redline for negotiation.

[34:00] Olivia (Hera): procurement wants to know if there are reseller/marketplace billing options because internal purchasing is easier through cloud marketplace.
[34:12] Sophie (Redwood): we support marketplace billing on AWS and GCP for hosted; pricing differs slightly, but it's an option. we'll call out invoice path tradeoffs in the pricing sheet.

[36:40] Samir (Hera): finance also wants to know sign-off thresholds — is legal approval sufficient for pilot or do we need executive sign-off?
[36:55] Olivia (Hera): procurement threshold is $75k; above that we need VP approval. pilot is expected below but if costs push up we'll escalate.

[39:00] Marco (Redwood): next on technical: Marco will run a 24-hour synthetic run with your sample prompt set to estimate token mix, latency, and egress. will include dedicated vs hosted cost per token.
[39:16] Ethan (Hera): we'll drop prompt set in the shared drive after the call.

[41:20] Sophie (Redwood): recap: we'll send DPA redline, annotated pricing & invoice sample, KMS/HSM options doc, audit-log spec, and a pilot cost model. you'll send legal exceptions and prompt set. we'll reconvene week of 7/28.
[41:45] Daniel (Hera): sounds good — please flag any non-negotiable items up front.
[42:00] Priya (Hera): one last note: if you can provide a short security one-pager for our SOC2 team that would speed review.
[42:10] Marco (Redwood): yes we have a SOC2 one-pager, will attach.

[44:00] Olivia (Hera): thanks all, looks like clear actions.
[44:05] Sophie (Redwood): thanks everyone — sending materials by next week, follow-up meeting invite pending.
[44:12] [meeting ends — recording stops]

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-attributions and small transcription errors; links referenced during meeting: DPA redline (link), pricing spreadsheet (link), pilot prompt set (drive link), SOC2 one-pager (link).
